The pattern was found through graph analysis linking current device usage to historical closed cases exhibiting identical device fan-out characteristics.

case.summary: This case was triggered by an analyst request monitoring a specific device profile used across 28 cards in Nov-Dec via an anonymous proxy. The graph showed the device profile 'SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080' linked to multiple other cards and confirmed historical fraud cases. The verdict is fraud with a final probability of 0.9, driven by the coordinated device fan-out pattern matching known schemes. Actions taken include creating the case, monitoring connected cards, escalating to an analyst, recommending card blocking under policy 6, and filing a report under policy 3a, R6, and R9.

sar.narrative: A suspicious online transaction involving customer C10326 and card C10326-K1 was flagged on 2016-11-14 at 16:54:00 for the amount of 159.3 USD in billing region 181. The activity was conducted through an online channel using product code C, with a primary email domain of yahoo.com and a recovery email domain of anonymous.com. The fraud was carried out using a new device profile, SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080, operating behind an anonymous proxy IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS. The total exposure amount for the affected transactions is 262.92 USD, comprising transaction 3457285 (159.30 USD) and transaction 3457521 (103.62 USD). This activity is suspicious because the mobile device profile fan-out lookup confirmed it was used across 20 cards between 2016-11-14 and 2016-11-24, always marked as new and behind an anonymous proxy, linking it to four confirmed closed cases. Initial and final fraud probabilities were assessed at 0.9. Automated actions executed included creating the case, monitoring connected cards, and escalating to an analyst, while recommendations were made to block the card (pending approval under policy 6) and file a regulatory report (pending approval under policy 3a, R6, and R9).
